consolidation_breakout.description: A second way in, for when AAVE never comes back down to its average: buy the break out of a quiet band.
consolidation_breakout.condition: The 24 bars before the current one sit inside a band no wider than 2% (highest high / lowest low - 1). The first bar to close above that band's top is the break; 60 minutes later the 1-minute close must still be above the top, and the buy lands on the next minute's open. Only the first break of each quiet stretch counts.
consolidation_breakout.market_filter: Only the blocked hours are shared with the dip rule. The downtrend filter is deliberately NOT applied: requiring the averages to be stacked upward before a break screens out exactly the breaks that start a new trend.

exit.note: A break comes out of a quiet band rather than a dip, so it carries its own tighter stop and its own trail.

trailing_stop.note: The arm was raised from +1.276% to +1.75% in September 2026. It applies to DIP lots only - a Mode C lot keeps its own +1.283% arm, where the later arm was measured to do nothing.

portfolio.sizing_rule: Each coin gets lot size x lots from the free USDT in the Binance wallet. A trade buys exactly one full lot when the coin has a free slot and Binance has at least one lot of free USDT; smaller amounts are never traded.

provenance.backtest_bnb_fees: Oct 2024 - Sep 2026 on $300 as 3 x $100 lots. With the deployed +1.276% arm: +$115.91 over 289 trades (255 dip, 34 breakout) at an 85.1% win rate, max drawdown -7.88%, five of six walk-forward windows. With the +1.75% arm now deployed, the same period gives +$116.37 over 271 trades at 79.3%, walk-forward +$123.62 against +$104.19, better in six of six windows, at a -10.23% mark-to-market drawdown. The breakout alone: 38 trades, +$24.44, an 89.5% win rate, six of six windows and a -1.36% drawdown.
provenance.caveats: A trend exit (Mode A) was tested and deliberately left out. On paper it added about $100, but a walk-forward selection test put its honest contribution at $2: the gain came from a few large moves in the first year and the right line length could not have been chosen in advance (16h +$169, 24h +$206, 36h +$124 - a spike, not a plateau). AAVE wins small and often, which is what the giveback trailing stop is for. Mode C, by contrast, improved four of six windows at every setting tested.
provenance.arm_change: Sept 2026 recheck: every other deployed setting was confirmed, but the dip's trail armed too early. Walk-forward rises steadily with the arming level - +1.276% $104.19, +1.5% $111.54, +1.75% $123.62, +2% $141.19, +2.25% $164.60, +2.5% $177.11 - and inside a pre-committed range of no more than double the deployed arm, choosing honestly beat leaving it alone ($126.02 against $104.19), the only setting change in the whole research programme to pass that gate. +1.75% was chosen as the conservative point: better in 6 of 6 walk-forward windows (+1.17, +0.28, +0.28, +2.50, +3.95, +11.24 = +$19.43 on $300) at a -10.23% mark-to-market drawdown against -9.62%. The cost is win rate: 85.2% -> 79.3%, fewer and larger wins. The gain is entirely in the dip lots ($100.78 -> $120.77 over the full window); Mode C is unaffected and its own arm was left alone. An ATR-scaled arm reaches the same place (0.4x ATR = about +2.9%) and adds nothing over a fixed number, so the fixed number is used.
